expanded_element.title: The Benefits of Lab-Grown Diamonds: A Comprehensive Guide
expanded_element.snippet: Lab-created diamonds have clear advantages: they cost less, and their origin is documented. They suit buyers who care about beauty, price, and knowing where a stone came from. Some buyers prefer a lab-grown diamond and some prefer a mined one.

expanded_element.snippet: The material 'diamond' is defined as carbon atoms in a cubic structure; both natural and synthetic diamonds are made of this material.
related_searches: What are synthetic diamonds made of?

expanded_element.title: Types of Lab-Grown Diamonds: HPHT vs CVD | The Diamond Guys
expanded_element.snippet: There are two main growth methods for real lab-grown diamonds: HPHT (High Pressure High Temperature) and CVD (Chemical Vapour Deposition). Separately there are diamond simulants - cubic zirconia, moissanite and Diamond Nexus - which look like diamonds but are not diamonds.
related_searches: What are the different types of synthetic diamonds?

expanded_element.title: Synthetic diamond | Definition, Techniques, & Facts | Britannica
expanded_element.snippet: Because synthesis is an expensive process, large stones of gem quality are rarely made. Instead, most synthetic diamond is produced as grit or small crystals that are used to provide hard coatings for industrial equipment such as grinding wheels, machine tools, wire-drawing dies, quarrying saws, and mining drills.
related_searches: What are the uses of synthetic diamonds?

expanded_element.title: What Is a Lab-Grown Diamond? History & Background - VRAI
expanded_element.snippet: The History of Lab-Grown Diamonds Timeline 1954: The first lab-grown diamond is created using the HPHT method. 1971: The first gem-quality lab-grown diamond is made. 1980s: The CVD method is further developed. Lab-grown diamond jewelry and engagement rings become widely available.
